page: Amazon Web Services r8gn.4xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and custom AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processors. It features 16 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz with a single thread per core, utilizing the arm64 architecture. The CPU configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core, and does not include local storage or integrated GPUs.

The r8gn.4xlarge provides a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps and is optimized for Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS). In memory benchmarks, the instance demonstrates strong capabilities, with Passmark memory scores reaching the top tier (top 10%). Large-block memory bandwidth read and write operations both rank in the strong category (top 25%), though small-block cached read bandwidth remains in the average tier.

General compute benchmarks, including stress-ng, Geekbench, and Passmark CPU tests, consistently place the Neoverse-V2 processor in the average performance tier. Text processing and database operations show stronger results, ranking in the top 25%. However, the instance exhibits performance limitations in large-scale machine learning tasks. Large language model (LLM) text generation speeds for both small (135M) and large (70B) models fall into the poor category (bottom 10%), indicating a clear tradeoff when using this hardware profile for generative AI workloads.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory density of 8.0 GB per core combined with the power-efficient ARMv9 architecture offers a balanced resource profile for memory-bound workloads without the overhead of x86 licensing. This server is suited for database operations, memory-intensive caching layers, text processing pipelines, and general-purpose web serving that requires high network throughput and substantial memory capacity.
